1.why: reset-validate and password-update require the submitted token to equal session.resetToken issued only for that session’s successful mock-account request.

2.why: resetToken is stored only on the requesting session, so another session/user cannot use that same code.

3.why: password-update only mutates the current session and never invalidates or deletes other entries in the sessions Map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS certs, localHttpsRequest/HSTS enforce HTTPS, but no explicit minimum TLS version is set in code.

5.why: passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but reset tokens and session fields are stored in memory as plaintext, not encrypted.

6.why: no real email is sent; API copy is generic and does not include profile PII, though the mock token is returned to the client.

7.why: email/token/password inputs are type-checked and validated, body size-capped, and the UI builds nodes with textContent rather than raw HTML.

8.why: no user-controlled redirect targets exist; navigation is client-side screen switches and fixed same-origin API paths.

9.why: there are no email templates that interpolate user HTML/scripts; delivery is only a simulated client log string.

10.why: mockDeliveryToken and mockMfaCode are returned in JSON and written into the on-page logs UI, so tokens are visibly exposed.

11.why: password hashes use bcrypt, but MFA_CODE is a hardcoded secret in source and reset tokens sit unencrypted in session state.

12.why: the fixed MFA_CODE "482913" acts as a default shared verification credential for every successful reset.

13.why: rateAllowed limits reset requests (3/15m), reset-code guesses (5/15m), and MFA attempts (5/15m) with 429 responses.

14.why: reset-request always returns the same generic message regardless of whether the email matches MOCK_ACCOUNT_EMAIL.

15.why: reset codes are 32-byte crypto random base64url values bound to the issuing session and single-use with expiry.
